acceptanceCriteria: The taskLexicalTerms doc comment in internal/contextindex/taskcontext.go describes the term table's actual tokenisation: termCounter.count (termtable.go) splits a body identifier at a lower-to-upper camelCase boundary, so `stripFinalNewline` is not one body token.

A test states which tables the whole-identifier task term (for example `stripfinalnewline`) can match in the posting walk. Either it is removed, because it can match no table, or the test names the table it matches and shows that the match reaches a posting.
body: Filed 2026-09-23 from the independent review of V1-0205/V1-0206 (TCP-V0-047 routing idf floor). The taskLexicalTerms comment says the term table tokenises a source body as ASCII runs, so `stripFinalNewline` in a body is the one token `stripfinalnewline`. termCounter.count (internal/contextindex/termtable.go, around lines 480-495) splits at a lower-to-upper boundary, so the body table holds `strip`, `final`, `newline` and not the compound. V1-0205 made instruction routing skip task terms the body table does not hold. The same compound still enters the lexical posting walk, and it is unconfirmed whether any table (path, symbol or body) can match it. Whether that walk gains anything from it is an open question.
